working:
Let the intercepts of the plane on the coordinate axes be $a$, $b$, and $c$, so that the vertices are $A(a, 0, 0)$, $B(0, b, 0)$, and $C(0, 0, c)$.

The centroid $G$ of $\triangle ABC$ is given by:
$$G = \left(\dfrac{a}{3}, \dfrac{b}{3}, \dfrac{c}{3}\right) = (1, 2, 2)$$

Equating coordinates:
$$a = 3, \quad b = 6, \quad c = 6$$

Thus, $A = (3, 0, 0)$, $B = (0, 6, 0)$, and $C = (0, 0, 6)$.

The vectors representing two sides of $\triangle ABC$ from $A$ are:
$$\vec{AB} = -3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}$$
$$\vec{AC} = -3\hat{i} + 6\hat{k}$$

Their cross product is:
$$\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -3 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 36\hat{i} + 18\hat{j} + 18\hat{k}$$

The magnitude of the cross product is:
$$|\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}| = \sqrt{36^2 + 18^2 + 18^2} = 18\sqrt{2^2 + 1^2 + 1^2} = 18\sqrt{6}$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}|\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}| = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 18\sqrt{6} = 9\sqrt{6}$$

Independent check: Centroid (1,2,2) gives intercepts A(3,0,0), B(0,6,0), C(0,0,6). AB=(-3,6,0), AC=(-3,0,6); AB×AC=(36,18,18), |AB×AC|=√1944=18√6, so area = ½·18√6 = 9√6.
